answer: Each identity registers one oasis well, locks a 70-credit bond, and fits its cap with a key-bound ivory seal. Each epoch the holder files a water-table reading; an auditor recomputes it from the glacier melt table and well depth, and a reading off by over 5 percent, a reused seal, or a duplicated well burns the bond. The first filing costs 34 credits, the kth 34+6(k-1), the 1000th 6028; 1000 fakes pay 3,031,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-well ring fails because a borrowed seal key mismatches the registered well key. An honest holder pays 34 once and recovers the bond after a clean audit.
